title: Contextual Slice Replay Orchestration and Anchoring Playbook
author: Marisol Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the orchestration pattern we use to reliably replay workload slices through the eval harness and to anchor slice-level baselines across model promotions, quantization changes, and serving runtime updates. It combines deterministic replay, stochastic resampling, and anchor scoring so teams can detect, localize, and triage regressions with high signal-to-noise and consistent instrumentation.

Purpose:
- Provide a reproducible, operationalized pattern for slice extraction, replay orchestration, and anchor creation.
- Ensure slice baselines are portable across environments (shadow, dedicated, hosted) and model variants (float, quantized).
- Reduce regression triage time by surfacing causal candidates and providing pre-baked diffs for human review.

Scope:
- Applies to: interactive generation and chat workloads, embedding batches with context metadata, and reranking pipelines where per-request context affects outputs.
- Not in scope: low-level kernel tuning, hardware provisioning, or privacy-incompatible datasets (see privacy-first-shadow-eval page for those).

Key definitions:
- Slice: a named subset of traffic defined by metadata predicates (intent, language, client_id, prompt_template, context_window).
- Replay Job: an orchestrated execution of a slice through a target model/config combo in the eval harness.
- Anchor: a compact summary of prior-run outputs and metrics used as a stable baseline for monitoring and comparison.
- Anchor Score: multidimensional metric vector (accuracy proxy, semantic drift, response-stability-index, token-cost) used to detect changes.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Slice owner: product/feature team that defines the slice semantics and acceptance criteria. (Primary contact required)
- Eval harness owner: eng applied-ml team — maintains replay infra, scheduler, and artifact storage.
- Regression triage owner: model reliability squad — drives investigation workflows and rollbacks.

Data and artifact requirements:
- Inputs: canonicalized request objects (JSONL), tokenizer metadata, KV-cache seeds for long-context tests, and deterministic RNG seeds where sampling is allowed.
- Outputs: model responses (text/structured), logits or top-k token distribution (when available), embedding vectors, and per-request telemetry (latency, cost, route).
- Storage: run artifacts are persisted in the eval-artifacts bucket under /slices/{slice_name}/{run_id}/ with an index.json manifest.

Slice definition matrix (example):
| Slice name | Predicate | Purpose | Min sample | Owner |
| Critical-invoice-phrases | language=en AND intent=invoice AND prompt_template=invoice-summarize | Business-critical NLU checks | 500 | BillingFE |
| Low-resource-lang-zh | language=zh AND client_tier=free | Coverage for low-resource tokens | 200 | i18n |
| Long-context-chats | context_tokens>2048 AND interaction_type=chat | KV cache and attention stability | 300 | ConversationalAI |

Replay orchestration procedure (step-by-step):
1. Slice registration: feature team registers slice in the Slice Registry with predicate, sample window, and TTL. Include a canonical prompt set (30–200 examples) and an acceptance rubric.
2. Sampling and seeding: the harness sampler pulls N requests according to the slice window and injects deterministic RNG seeds and KV-cache seeds. For stochastic anchors, include M resamples per request (default M=3).
3. Environment mapping: map the target run to a model artifact (sha or model-id), quant-profile (if any), runtime image, and routing policy.
4. Dry-run validation: run a small pilot (10–20 requests) to validate tokenization parity and that no privacy flags are triggered.
5. Full replay: schedule the replay job on the eval cluster. Use priority queues for critical slices. Capture raw outputs, metadata, and system telemetry.
6. Anchor computation: compute anchor vectors (see Anchoring & Baselines) and persist alongside run artifacts.
7. Diff and alerting: compute delta vs. anchor and run automated checks. If thresholds exceeded, create a regression ticket with pre-populated findings.

Anchoring and baseline procedures:
- Anchor types:
  - Snapshot anchor: full-run anchor created at release cut and stored permanently.
  - Rolling anchor: windowed anchor computed over the latest X runs (default X=7) for stable slices.
  - Synthetic anchor: for small slices, generated by augmentation and weighted sampling.
- Anchor content: for each request store response hash, embedding centroid, top-5 token distributions, stability score, and cost per request.
- Anchor scoring (example calculation):
  - Response-stability-index (RSI) = fraction of requests with normalized similarity >= 0.85 (cosine for embeddings, BLEU/ROUGE/SemSim for text)
  - Semantic-drift = 1 - average cosine(embedding_current, embedding_anchor)
  - Token-cost-delta = (tokens_current - tokens_anchor)/tokens_anchor
- Anchor retention policy: Snapshot anchors retained indefinitely. Rolling anchors retained 90 days. Synthetic anchors retained 30 days.

Metrics, thresholds, and automated checks:
- Primary alarm triggers (per-slice):
  - RSI drop >= 0.10 => create P2 regression ticket.
  - Semantic-drift increase >= 0.08 => auto-run triage (bisect by model and quant-config).
  - Token-cost-delta >= 0.20 AND RSI drop >= 0.05 => flag for cost-quality tradeoff review.
  - Latency increase > 25% p50 or p95 breach => route to infra runbook.
- Evaluation metrics to compute per-run: RSI, semantic-drift, top-token-shift (KL divergence), fidelity score (task dependent), and end-to-end correctness (if labeled).

Integration with quantization profiles and runtime variants:
- Label each replay job with quant_profile_id and runtime_image. Store quantization metadata (bit-width, per-channel/per-tensor, calibration dataset id).
- Recommended workflow when testing quantized variants:
  1. Run float baseline anchor (if not present).
  2. Run deterministic quantized replay with identical seeds.
  3. Compute paired diffs and generate per-request failure indicators.
  4. If divergences exceed thresholds, run targeted per-layer micro-benchmarks and create a quant-failure case.
- Crossworkload guidance: for heterogeneous slices (e.g., embeddings + generation), anchor each signal type separately and compute a composite anchor score.

Regression triage fast-path (operational playbook):
1. Auto-classify: harness computes candidate root causes using heuristics (config mismatch, tokenizer drift, quantization delta, prompt template change, model version).
2. Automated bisect: run binary bisect across commits or model snapshots to narrow to a 1–2 commit window.
3. Localize to dimension: use per-request diffs to determine if failure is concentrated in prompts, languages, or client IDs.
4. Escalate: if auto-classify confidence < 0.7, escalate to model reliability squad with artifacts attached.
5. Rollback/mitigation: if slice is business-critical and impact > P1 thresholds, perform rollback to last snapshot anchor and notify SRE.

CLI / API examples:
- Create replay job (curl):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://eval-api.redwood.internal/v1/replay-jobs \
    -d '{"slice":"long-context-chats","model_id":"rwd-llama-70b-v2","quant_profile":"q8-perchannel-v2","sample_size":300,"seeds":{"deterministic":true}}'

- Example manifest (index.json) snippet stored with artifacts:
  {
    "run_id": "20260120-longcontext-01",
    "slice": "long-context-chats",
    "model_id": "rwd-llama-70b-v2",
    "quant_profile": "q8-perchannel-v2",
    "artifact_paths": ["responses.jsonl","topk.jsonl","metrics.json"]
  }

Rollout checklist for slice anchoring in release pipelines:
- [ ] Snapshot anchor exists for current main release.
- [ ] Canonical prompt set verified and annotated with acceptance rubric.
- [ ] Quant profiles and runtime labels included in job metadata.
- [ ] Low-latency dry-run passed.
- [ ] Automated checks and thresholds configured in monitoring.
- [ ] Regression triage playbook contact and runbook links attached.

Operational notes and best practices:
- Prefer deterministic seeds for regression-sensitive slices; allow stochastic resamples for robustness checks.
- Keep canonical prompt sets small (30–200) but representative; control for label imbalance.
- When possible, compute embedding-centroid deltas rather than raw text diffs for multilingual stability.
- Annotate expensive slices with cost-owners; include token-cost delta in decision heuristics.

Troubleshooting quick reference:
- Tokenization mismatch: run token-compare tool and inspect tokenizer version differences; common fix: pin tokenizer artifact in env mapping.
- Large semantic-drift with no conf change: check upstream prompt rewrite or client-side template changes.
- Quant-induced hallucination: escalate to quant team; run per-layer fp32-vs-quant attribution tests.

References and related pages:
- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting (internal) - for slice fingerprinting primitives.
- Quant profile synthesis and safety playbook - for quant test patterns and thresholds.
- Regression triage playbooks - for escalation and incident handling steps.

Appendix: example threshold table
| Metric | Warning | Action | Owner |
| RSI drop 0.05–0.10 | Create P3 ticket, run extended resample | Feature team + Eval harness |
| RSI drop >= 0.10 | Create P2 ticket, bisect | Model reliability squad |
| Semantic-drift 0.04–0.08 | Run embedding pair analysis | Applied-ML |
| Semantic-drift >= 0.08 | Auto-trigger bisect and escalate | Model reliability squad |
